notes: Fourth sweep (2026-10-22-c): five runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2) at head 3e3581d with no uncommitted changes; every run has rc 0, a model_id matching its tier, and skill_hash 03a6bb2b... which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the current idiomatic-elixir/, so all runs are graded against the current text.

Rule list: the eight rules whose index row names ecto-phoenix. git diff 0397dec -- idiomatic-elixir/ touches only SKILL.md, references/processes.md (the Use ETS example now names its options) and references/testing.md; references/ecto-phoenix.md is unchanged, so its six rules are graded to the 2026-10-22-b standard, and Keep migrations to schema changes also to check-7's reading: a separate script that uses MyApp.Blog.Post misses the case check, not the rule, which forbids schema modules only inside migrations (haiku-1 line 140: alias MyApp.Blog.Post).

Two rules changed since 0397dec by being added: Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call and Open a module with `use`, `import`, `alias`, `require`, in that order. Neither has a verdict in 2026-10-22-b, so both are graded to sweeps/2026-10-22-check-7/grades/ecto-phoenix-skill.json; their text is unchanged since b0bf52c, which recorded that batch (git diff b0bf52c HEAD -- idiomatic-elixir/ touches neither). The sentences that decide them: "When an argument is a map, struct or keyword list that would span several lines, build it first under a name that says what it is, write it one field per line, and set each multi-line statement apart with a blank line." and "Right after `@moduledoc`, group each kind together, in that order". As in check-7, a map the formatter keeps on one line is outside the first rule, a multi-line from/2 named before its Repo call counts as clean, and blank lines between directive groups are not required by the text.

The six ecto-phoenix.md rules: 0 of 5 violated, down from 2 of 5 (both Haiku, Keep migrations) in 2026-10-22-b. Every run casts only [:title, :body], declares assoc_constraint(:user) and sets user_id on the struct; every run uses Repo.transact/2 with a two-step with, preloads the author, keeps the migration to add :published_at, and shows via Blog.get_post!/1 over Repo.get!/2. Backfills: four scripts on the "posts" table (opus-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2) and one over MyApp.Blog.Post (haiku-1), which misses that case check.

other_violations follow the 2026-10-22-b standard: a missing @moduledoc on the context or a public context function without @doc counts; missing docs on schema modules, controllers and migrations does not (haiku-2's Post.changeset/2 and publish_changeset/2 have no @doc). None found: every MyApp.Blog has @moduledoc and @doc on each public function; no single-step pipe and no pipeline that starts with a call; every with has two steps; one-expression bodies kept in blocks (publish_changeset/2) are not required to use do:; no defstruct; no fn a capture would replace. The assumption comments above the audit-log helpers (opus-1 lines 113-114, haiku-1 106-107, haiku-2 125, sonnet-1 142-143, sonnet-2 111-112) and the migrations' pointers to the backfill script (haiku-1 126-127, haiku-2 37) say what the code cannot show, so they are not restating comments.

format_ok: result.json reports false for all five because plain mix format adds parentheses to the Ecto and Phoenix DSL calls. As in the previous sweeps, the grader recomputed it with Code.format_string!/2 and the DSL calls (field, belongs_to, timestamps, from, add, alter, execute and others) in locals_without_parens: all five pass, and no line exceeds 98 characters. Nothing compiles because Phoenix and Ecto are not installed.
